findings.text: `list_live()` is named as being "in `reckon/crew/routing.py`", but that module only imports it (routing.py:53); it is defined in `reckon/crew/runs.py:455`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — `list_live()` is attributed to `reckon/crew/routing.py` but is defined in `reckon/crew/plan_review`-unrelated `reckon/crew/runs.py:455` and only imported into routing.py (routing.py:53); the name resolves, so the anchor is usable, but it points a reader at the importer rather than the owner.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §2's done-when names two fixtures as controls: a collapsed-plan review that must be counted pre-collapse-only and lose coverage (positive), and a section-set-form review that must be counted as neither (negative); both are falsifiable against the census output.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the census report and its script are written under the run's own report directory, a durable path a later reader opens, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §2 introduces no code symbols; its §-references are the plan's own section ids, which the plan HTML owns.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated root cause matches the code: `_fingerprint_forms` (plan_review.py:678) returns three digests whose second is the declaration-keeping legacy form, `review_coverage` (plan_review.py:823-851) early-returns on a whole-plan match and otherwise falls to per-unit coverage, so withholding that form is a faithful simulation of §3's change; a scratch run over the plan under review confirms the mechanism produces its done-when — with `plan_fingerprint` set to forms[1] and stale stored unit digests, `review_coverage` reports `{_document, s2, s3}` uncovered only once the pre-collapse form is withheld, and a section-set-form record stays fully covered either way.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable, the read-only census; the retirement it gates is §3's separate goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §3 declares its dependency on §2 (`plan-section-depends-on {"s3": [the-fingerprint-has-one-form#s2]}`), and §2's read-only census needs no upstream node, so no dependency is missing or misdirected.
